hook.text: Probiotics are a $60 billion industry. But do the bacteria in your yogurt actually survive to reach your gut?

buildup.text: Probiotics are live microorganisms that provide health benefits when consumed in adequate amounts.

discovery.text: Some strains survive stomach acid and colonize the intestine. Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG is one of the most studied.

twist.text: Most probiotic products don't specify strain, dose, or survival rate. Many products deliver dead bacteria—zero benefit.

climax.text: Strong evidence supports probiotics for antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Evidence for most other claims is weak.

punchline.text: Some probiotics work. Most products are wishful thinking. Strain matters.

quiz.question: What is the strongest evidence-backed use of probiotics?
